patient.name: Dorothy Vance
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe shortness of breath, unable to lie flat

history.hpi: Husband reports increasing shortness of breath and orthopnea over the past 6 hours, now unable to lie flat or speak in full sentences. Productive cough with pink, frothy sputum since roughly 3 AM. Husband states she missed her furosemide dose yesterday.
history.lastOralIntake: Sip of water around 9 PM; no food since dinner
history.events: Husband called 911 after her breathing worsened and she began coughing up pink sputum around 3 AM

scene.location: Single-story home, patient found sitting upright in a recliner in the living room, unable to lie flat
scene.bystanders: Husband present, called 911 after her breathing worsened overnight
visualCues: Patient tripod-sitting in recliner, using accessory muscles
Pink, frothy sputum at corners of mouth
Home oxygen concentrator and nebulizer present but unused tonight

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find an 81-year-old female in severe respiratory distress, tripod-sitting, with audible rales and pink frothy sputum. She is hypertensive and tachycardic, consistent with acute decompensated heart failure.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Labored, accessory muscle use, bilateral rales to mid-lung fields
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, bounding, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Productive cough with pink frothy sputum

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply CPAP for severe respiratory distress with hypoxia; coach patient through mask seal
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) should be considered early for severe respiratory distress or impending respiratory failure The key to successful use of NIV in a patient who has not used it before is coaching and explanation of the process and reassurance of the patient
expectedActions.rationale: Early NIV restores oxygenation and reduces work of breathing in cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL for SBP ≥160/MAP >120; may repeat every 5 min if SBP remains >100 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP >= 160 mmHg or MAP greater than 120: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: High-dose nitrates reduce preload and afterload, improving pulmonary edema in severely hypertensive CHF.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: Crew applies CPAP for severe respiratory distress with hypoxia and administers nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL per the SBP ≥160 mmHg / MAP >120 dosing tier.
Crew repeats the nitroglycerin dose on the 5-minute timer without first rechecking blood pressure, missing the SBP >100 mmHg requirement for repeat dosing.

phases.name: CPAP and high-dose nitro started
phases.description: CPAP is applied and coached, and high-dose nitroglycerin is given for the severely hypertensive presentation. Initial response is favorable — oxygenation and work of breathing improve.
phases.triggerCondition: After CPAP is applied and the patient is coached through the mask seal, nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL is given per the SBP ≥160 mmHg / MAP >120 tier, repeatable every 5 minutes if SBP remains above 100 mmHg.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Improved, less accessory muscle use, rales persist but decreasing
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, skin still diaphoretic but color improving
otherFindings: Patient able to speak short sentences between breaths

expectedActions.shortAction: Hold further nitroglycerin; SBP 92 mmHg is below the >100 mmHg threshold required to repeat
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Nitroglycerin 0.8 mg SL, can repeat every 5 minutes for SBP greater than 100 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Repeating nitroglycerin below the SBP threshold would worsen hypotension in a preload-dependent, volume-depleted patient.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

expectedActions.shortAction: IV fluid bolus 250-500 mL for SBP <100 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP less than 100 mmHg: IV fluid bolus 250–500 mL
expectedActions.rationale: The protocol directs a fluid bolus for hypotensive pulmonary edema patients regardless of underlying cause, since preload augmentation is needed once nitrate-driven venodilation causes hypotension.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: Crew rechecks blood pressure before the next scheduled nitroglycerin dose, as required by the repeat-dosing threshold, and finds the patient has become hypotensive.
The crew recognizes the hypotension but does not administer the indicated fluid bolus, allowing perfusion to continue deteriorating.

phases.name: SBP reassessed before repeat nitro
phases.description: Reassessment before the scheduled repeat nitroglycerin dose reveals the patient has become hypotensive — a known risk in this volume-depleted, diuretic-treated elderly patient. Further nitroglycerin is appropriately withheld.
phases.triggerCondition: Blood pressure reassessment ahead of the next nitroglycerin dose shows SBP has fallen to 92 mmHg, below the SBP >100 mmHg threshold required to repeat dosing, in a patient who is volume-depleted from chronic diuretic therapy and a missed furosemide dose.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weaker, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact, slightly slower to respond
otherFindings: SBP now below the repeat-dosing threshold

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain continuous CPAP mask seal through transport; do not break seal until ED handoff
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: DO NOT discontinue CPAP/BiPAP until patient is on the emergency department stretcher and hospital CPAP/BiPAP is immediately available for patient to be switched over, or physician is at bedside and requesting CPAP/BiPAP be discontinued. Breaking the mask seal causes a significant decrease in airway pressures and may lead to abrupt decompensation due to atelectasis and alveolar collapse.
expectedActions.rationale: Breaking the CPAP seal, even briefly, risks abrupt decompensation from atelectasis.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess full vital signs and mental status serially en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full set of vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment), temperature, and O2 saturation
expectedActions.rationale: Serial reassessment catches recurrent hypotension or re-accumulating pulmonary edema before it becomes critical.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

transitions.condition: A 250-500 mL IV fluid bolus is administered per the SBP <100 mmHg guidance, and perfusion improves while CPAP is maintained.

phases.name: Fluid bolus given for hypotension
phases.description: Following the fluid bolus, blood pressure recovers while CPAP and oxygenation are maintained. Patient is packaged for transport with continuous reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: After the 250-500 mL fluid bolus, SBP recovers above 100 mmHg with the CPAP seal maintained throughout and oxygenation continuing to improve.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Much improved, minimal accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong, skin warming, diaphoresis resolving
otherFindings: CPAP seal maintained continuously since application
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I can breathe so much better now, thank you."

phases.name: Nitro repeated without BP recheck
phases.description: The crew repeats the nitroglycerin dose purely on the 5-minute timer without rechecking blood pressure first. Hypotension develops unrecognized and progresses further than it should have.
phases.triggerCondition: Nitroglycerin is redosed at the 5-minute mark without a blood pressure recheck, missing the SBP >100 mmHg requirement for repeat dosing; the patient becomes progressively more hypotensive before the crew notices.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and thready, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Hypotension unrecognized until mental status declined
No fluid bolus or nitro hold in place

expectedActions.shortAction: Norepinephrine 1.2 mcg/min IV (62 kg × 0.02 mcg/kg/min), titrate to SBP >90 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Unrecognized, worsening nitro-induced hypotension now requires pressor support after fluid alone is unlikely to be sufficient given the delay.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)

phases.name: Fluid bolus withheld
phases.description: The crew recognizes the hypotension but does not give the indicated fluid bolus. Perfusion continues to deteriorate.
phases.triggerCondition: Hypotension is identified but the indicated 250-500 mL fluid bolus is not administered, allowing perfusion to worsen further.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Improved on CPAP but patient increasingly lethargic
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: SBP continuing to trend downward without intervention

expectedActions.shortAction: IV fluid bolus 250-500 mL now indicated for worsening SBP <100 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: SBP less than 100 mmHg: IV fluid bolus 250–500 mL
expectedActions.rationale: Delayed correction of nitrate-induced hypotension allows preventable hypoperfusion to worsen.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Respiratory Distress (includes Bronchospasm, Pulmonary Edema)
